title: California Republic
capsule: The California Republic — popularly the Bear Flag Republic — existed for just 25 days, from June 14 to July 9, 1846, when a group of American settlers seized Sonoma from Mexican authorities, raised a flag bearing a grizzly bear and star, and declared independence from Mexico. William B. Ide served as its commander and chief, with U.S. Army Captain John C. Frémont covertly encouraging the revolt; no civil governance structure was ever established before the republic dissolved. On July 9, 1846, U.S. Navy Lieutenant Joseph Revere arrived with American flags and orders confirming U.S. annexation of California during the Mexican–American War, replacing the Bear Flag at the Sonoma plaza. The Bear Flag design nonetheless became the basis for California's official state flag.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The geographic extent — roughly north of San Francisco Bay — is documented in contemporary military dispatches, though never formally demarcated.
